name: Oirat Confederation (17th century)
alt: Oirat union of the Dzungar basin

predecessors.name: Four Oirats
predecessors.text: the Oirat lands of western Mongolia and the Altai that the Eastern Mongols 'pushed ... westward' from 1480

successors.name: Dzungar Khanate
successors.text: the Dzungarian core on the upper Emil River and the Junggar basin, 365,737 km2

successors.name: Khoshut Khanate
successors.text: Qinghai (Koke Nuur) and then Tibet, where 'Gushi Khan went ... in 1636' with 10,000 Oirats

successors.name: Kalmyk Khanate
successors.text: the lower Volga where the Torghut and Dorbets settled in 1630

ledger.x: 1609: the Oirat realm of Dzungaria enters the map.
1628: the Torghut and Dorbets leave for the Volga.
1634: the Oirat Confederation gives way to the Dzungar Khanate.

wars.name: Oirat-Khalkha wars
wars.outcome: No frontier moved: the Khalkha 'repeatedly launched massive attacks on the Oirats' (1552-1628), looting the Irtysh, Barkol and Altai; the Oirats crushed the Khalkha prince Sholoi Ubashi 'perhaps around 1623'; peace with the Khalkha came after Ligdan Khan died…

wars.name: Oirat campaigns against the Kazakhs and Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz, subjugating them in the process'; no land is named and no border moved.

certainty.note: Pastoral frontiers in the Junggar basin and the Tian Shan; no page describes a boundary.
